newsitem.title: GREECE: OLYMPIC AIRWAYS FEARS NO OUTSIDE COMPETITION - MIN.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPIC AIRWAYS FEARS NO OUTSIDE COMPETITION - MIN.

text.p: The deregulation of Europe's air transport holds no fears for Olympic Airways, Greece's national carrier, Transport and Communications Minister Haris Kastanidis said.
"Olympic Airways (OA), given the structure of the Greek market, will not face any essential competition from foreign firms," Kastanidis told financial weekly 'Ekonomikos Tahydromos'.
The idiosyncracies of the Greek market, such as the large number of islands, guarantee that after a short transitional period, the market will right itself anew with OA in control, he said.

Kastanidis said the national carrier had made progress in the context of the European Union's 1994 reform programme particularly in the sectors of profits, commercial policies - including new routes to Central and Eastern Europe - fleet planning and organisational restructuring.
"Olympic Airways has understood that a basic factor for survival and development in the increasingly competitive environment is the reduction of its operating costs," he said.
"This requires an improvement in the level of services offered, increased productivity, better marketing and more careful investment planning," he added.
